title: In these or those: näissä, noissa, niissä
summary: Recognise and produce the plural inessive demonstrative forms.
objectives: Connect näissä, noissa, and niissä with plural reference.
Use the forms independently for several bounded containers.
Contrast singular and plural inessive forms.

sections.title: See the pattern
paragraphs: The plural inessive demonstratives are näissä, noissa, and niissä.
They can mean in these/those/them when the context explicitly supplies several containers, groups, or bounded areas.

sections.title: Use one clear decision
paragraphs: The plural subject in the examples uses ovat.
Each independent example identifies the intended containers or areas before the Finnish sentence. Compare tässä with näissä, tuossa with noissa, and siinä with niissä.

examples.english: Cars are in those over there.
steps: Context: the speaker indicates the farther, jointly visible bounded container or area.
Autot: the complete plural form is supplied.
noissa: learned inessive form of nuo.
Context: both people already know which bounded container or area is meant.
Autot: the complete plural form is supplied.
niissä: learned inessive form of ne.
Context: both people already know which bounded container or area is meant.
Talot: the complete plural form is supplied.
näissä: learned inessive form of nämä.

commonMistakes: Do not use tässä for several containers.
Do not confuse noissa with nuo.
Do not substitute the broader adverbs täällä, tuolla, or siellä.

practiceExercises.instruction: Put the words in the correct order.
practiceExercises.prompt: Context: Several storage compartments are open. The speaker indicates the nearby compartments. Optional practice: Build “Keys are in these.” At a school entrance. Start from nämä (“these”). Use the supplied subject avaimet (“keys”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Näissä is the inessive form of nämä and expresses a bounded inside or immediately located relation.

practiceExercises.prompt: Context: Several storage compartments are open. The speaker indicates the farther-away compartments, visible to both people. Optional practice: Choose the sentence that means “Keys are in those over there.” While sorting objects. Start from nuo (“those over there”). Use the supplied subject avaimet (“keys”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Noissa is the inessive form of nuo and expresses a bounded inside or immediately located relation.

sentenceExplanation.translation: Keys are in those over there.
sentenceExplanation.pattern: subject being located + linking verb + inessive demonstrative location

parts.formation: the complete plural form is supplied

Correct. Noissa is the inessive form of nuo and expresses a bounded inside or immediately located relation.
“näissä” is the plural inessive form linked to nämä; use “noissa”, the plural inessive form linked to nuo.
“niissä” is the plural inessive form linked to ne; use “noissa”, the plural inessive form linked to nuo.
“nuo” is a plural nominative form for farther, jointly visible referents; use “noissa”, the plural inessive form linked to nuo.
